section_1.title: The Architecture Landscape (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Define the Transformer's two main components: Attention (the router) and MLPs (the storage). Introduce the metaphor of a library where Attention finds the book, but the MLP contains the ink on the pages.
section_1.example: Imagine a librarian (Attention) finding the encyclopedia on 'Mammals', while the MLP is the specific paragraph inside defining what a 'Dog' is.

section_2.title: The Key-Value Memory Mechanism (0:45-2:00)
section_2.content: Explain the MLP as a collection of 'Key-Value' memories. Visualize a matrix multiplication as an operation where input vectors (keys) are matched against stored patterns, triggering an output vector (value) that reinforces a specific fact.
section_2.example: Visualizing a grid of light bulbs: Inputting 'Tokyo' activates a specific pattern of lights that, when summed, glows with the brightness of 'Japan'.

section_3.title: Weight Updates: Writing the Fact (2:00-3:30)
section_3.content: Describe how gradient descent 'writes' facts into weights. When the model sees (Subject: Paris, Relation: Capital Of, Object: France), it modifies the MLP weights to bridge these concepts. Explain this as adjusting the 'stiffness' of a connection.
section_3.example: Using a slider analogy: Adjusting a fader on a mixing board until the output 'France' becomes louder when 'Paris' is triggered.

section_4.title: Retrieval and Generalization (3:30-4:30)
section_4.content: Explain how the model generalizes. Because facts are stored as distributed weights, the model can infer relationships it hasn't seen explicitly, effectively 'reasoning' through overlapping patterns in the vector space.
section_4.example: If the model knows 'A tiger is a cat' and 'Cats are mammals', the overlapping activation patterns allow the model to categorize the tiger correctly without a direct database lookup.

section_5.title: Summary & Reflection (4:30-5:00)
section_5.content: Recap: Attention is for context, MLPs are for static knowledge. Final note on how this makes models 'black boxes'—it's hard to find the specific neuron that stores 'the capital of France' because the knowledge is diffused.
section_5.example: Comparing the MLP to a hologram: You can break off a piece of the film (the weights), and you still see the whole image, just slightly blurrier.
